summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey puts AI use in transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) at 13.0% of firms in the latest period, up from 7.9% in the prior period. The measure is narrow: firms answering yes to whether the business used AI in the last two weeks. The question was first asked in September 2023, so the series is young and the comparison is short. Read plainly, roughly one in eight transportation and warehousing firms reports recent AI use, which makes this a sector where adoption is real but far from universal.

What the cited sources show is that the deployments cluster in specific functions rather than spreading evenly. Aurora describes self-driving freight built on the Aurora Driver, with a hybrid model pairing professional drivers with autonomous hauling on long-haul routes. Samsara describes a connected operations platform that analyzes the data it collects, with AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, dash cams, drowsiness detection and driver coaching. C.H. Robinson describes autonomous logistics orchestration in which the supply chain analyzes, decides, executes and improves across every shipment, and runs an AI assistant on its site. Wärtsilä points to AI-driven predictive analytics alongside low and zero carbon engines for marine customers, and Airbus frames autonomy and digitised operations as part of its aerospace innovation work. Waymo's safety page describes a fully autonomous ride-hailing service and a published safety program.

The vendor and money picture concentrates among large operators and equipment makers. Samsara says its platform helps 20,000+ operations and credits its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts and automated coaching with 380,000+ accidents prevented. Aurora's page carries endorsements from Werner and from Volvo, whose VNL Autonomous integrates the Aurora Driver. C.H. Robinson positions itself as a third party logistics and supply chain management provider whose scale and data underpin its orchestration pitch. Wärtsilä describes itself as a global leader in technologies and lifecycle solutions for marine and energy markets. The American Trucking Associations, with more than 37,000 members, is the trade body in the room on trucking policy.

ROI evidence in these pages is mostly operator-reported rather than independently audited. Samsara's 380,000+ accidents prevented figure is its own. Aurora's page quotes a customer calling early pilot results impressive, specifically autonomous hauling between Fort Worth and El Paso, and quotes a driver saying the technology gives drivers better lives by handling lengthier and less desirable routes. Waymo's safety hub is described in this site's curated points as the most complete public evidence base from an AV operator, with published methodology and crash-rate comparisons. None of the cited pages offers a cost-per-mile or payback figure a buyer could plug into a budget.

The regulatory posture is still being written and is largely voluntary. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 sets out the agency's vision for safety and ethical considerations in aviation AI, with an action plan, anticipated rulemaking and annual amendment. The International Maritime Organization adopted a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in May 2026, effective 1 July 2026, providing voluntary guidance for safe design, operation and certification, technology-neutral and intended to facilitate a future transition into a mandatory instrument. The IMO states that at present there are no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships that operate autonomously or remotely controlled, though trials have shown larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible. Earlier trials ran under interim guidelines approved by the Maritime Safety Committee in June 2019. This site's curated points place the FAA's innovation work and EASA's roadmap as the regulatory record for AI flight systems and eVTOL certification, and the ATA as the body tracking autonomous freight policy.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material suggests separating the visible frontier from the ordinary case. The Census Bureau figure of 13.0% describes the average firm, while the named deployments come from large carriers, brokers, equipment makers and platform vendors with the data and capital to run them. The safety and efficiency claims in these pages come from the companies selling or operating the systems, and the rules that would govern aviation and maritime autonomy are either roadmaps or voluntary codes rather than settled mandatory law. A deployment decision here rests on function-level fit, on whether the vendor's own metrics can be verified against your operation, and on how much regulatory change you can absorb while the frameworks mature.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä claims it is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company says it already has most of the technology needed to decarbonise, from engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to AI-driven predictive analytics. Wärtsilä is using these tools to help customers take the next step on their decarbonisation journey.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The site catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, giving each model's licence, download count and release date, and says the list is refreshed daily. It states the catalogue is built from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, with every model linking to its own Hub page. The page records that it was last verified on 2026-09-27. The same database, it says, also underlies its coverage of state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators and weekly digests.
